package_info.package_name: Preinstalled HiddenAds Malware on UMX Mobile Phones
package_info.why_malicious: The preinstalled application is a variant of the HiddenAds malware family, embedded in the system partition of UMX U686CL mobile phones. It cannot be removed by the user, originates from an untrusted foreign source, and performs persistent ad fraud by displaying intrusive ads and communicating with remote servers without user consent, violating user privacy and device integrity.

execution_context.trigger: At device boot and during runtime

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At device boot and during runtime, the code schedules a persistent background service that establishes network connections to remote ad servers, retrieves ad content, and displays intrusive ad overlays on top of other apps, resulting in continuous ad fraud and user disruption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes automatically at boot and persists in the background, leveraging system-level permissions to display overlays and communicate with remote servers. It cannot be removed by the user, operates without user consent, and is embedded in the system partition, making it highly suspicious and malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate preinstalled system apps should not perform persistent, unremovable ad fraud, initiate background network activity to unknown servers, or display overlays without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate ad-supported apps may display ads, but only after user installation, with clear consent, and always allow uninstallation. They do not run as unremovable system apps or display overlays outside their own context.
key_indicators: System app embedded in /system/app/HiddenAds.apk performing ad-related activity
Automatic execution at device boot via RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED
Persistent background service with network communication to remote ad servers
Display of intrusive overlays using SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW permission
Unremovable by user through standard Android UI

attack_chain.action: Malicious app is preinstalled in the system partition of the device firmware, ensuring persistence and preventing user removal.
attack_chain.leads_to: Automatic execution at device boot and continuous presence on the device.

attack_chain.action: On boot and at regular intervals, the app initiates a background service that connects to remote ad servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Fetching and displaying intrusive ad overlays, generating fraudulent ad revenue and disrupting user experience.

behavioral_signatures: Unremovable system app with persistent background network activity to ad servers
Display of ad overlays outside of any user-initiated app context using SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW
Automatic execution at device boot via RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED broadcast receiver
file_indicators: System apps with obfuscated or generic names performing ad-related activity
Presence of system apps requesting SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and INTERNET permissions
network_indicators: Frequent outbound connections from system apps to known ad fraud or suspicious ad network domains
Unusual or high-volume network traffic originating from preinstalled system apps
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for system apps located in /system/app/ that cannot be uninstalled by the user and that request both SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and INTERNET permissions. Monitor for background network connections from these apps to ad servers, and detect overlays displayed outside of user-initiated app contexts. Use mobile security solutions to identify known HiddenAds variants and analyze system app behavior for persistent ad fraud patterns.
